original.target_description: Experiment 1: reported matrices solved after recalling books versus Ten Commandments, in the recycle/opportunity-to-cheat conditions; planned contrast in the full four-cell ANOVA.

n.sample_role: Participants in the focal books/recycle versus Commandments/recycle comparison. Original paper prints 229 students for the entire four-cell experiment but does not print the two focal cell counts; the contrast-specific analytic n is not established here.
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported for Experiment 1; separate recycle-cell sample sizes are not printed in the original article.

replication.target_description: Primary random-effects meta-analysis of the Commandments-cheat minus books-cheat difference in self-reported matrices solved, 19 eligible laboratories. Fig. 2 is on printed p. 306 (PDF p. 8); primary-results prose is on printed p. 304 (PDF p. 6).

n.sample_role: Analytic participants in Commandments-cheat and books-cheat respectively, across 19 laboratories; counts printed separately in Fig. 2. The 4,674 primary-analysis total includes control conditions and is not the n for this two-condition contrast.
n.exclusions: Primary eligibility: students aged 18–25, sample sex balance 20%–80% female, task adherence and completion; excluded incorrect administration and sessions under 50. Data-blind exceptions included seven samples over 80% female and one age exception. Fig. 2 counts are included participants after these rules.

reported_success.quote: This project replicated their procedures but did not find evidence of reduced cheating following the moral reminder.

notes: The two supplied records have the same neutral description and page locators, with no distinct outcome/test identifier. Both therefore use the recycle-condition moral-reminder contrast, rather than the four-cell interaction or religiosity/heterogeneity tests. Original n is null: the printed total of 229 is for all four cells, and no focal two-cell analytic count is printed in that paper. The original article prints F and rounded cell means, but no mean-difference effect estimate: retained printed F even for requested mean difference, without subtracting rounded means. The replication prints a mean difference and Cohen’s d but no focal test statistic or p; retained mean difference even for requested test statistic. Its p = .78 belongs to heterogeneity and p = .20 to religiousness moderation, so neither was assigned to the focal effect. Replication n retains separately printed condition counts without summing them. The RRR also reports original-study values in Fig. 2; these were not substituted for the original paper’s printed test. Full-text titles verified against both supplied references.
